analysis: All four units are documentation-only (docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/developer/test.md). No executable code, keys, wire contracts, attestation, authorization or encryption behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The changes are: a date bump; the Nemotron Super encoded-body ceiling in the inference.md patch excerpt (8 MiB to 40 MiB, with the over-limit error now media_too_large instead of the invalid-media 400); a note that JSON response_format may accompany tools (calls returned, otherwise validated as JSON); and two new test descriptions in test.md (NemotronSuperOpenRouterVideoTests, NemotronSuperOpenRouterCapabilityTests). The replayed head_text units for inference.md (lines 2039-2602) are surrounding unchanged text and the changed ranges lie outside them, so I could not verify those ranges directly. I did not verify the code behind the raised body ceiling. The 40 MiB figure is described as tied to the 25 MiB inline-media cap as base64, and memory admission still reserves a media charge (503 on failure) and caps the prompt at the context bound. Whether the real code enforces this and whether the ceiling raises DoS or memory exposure (T-007/T-010 class, TB-007) is a source-level question outside the supplied evidence. Nothing here weakens the prefix-cache threat T-041: the cache stays partitioned by authenticated scope, with no cache receipts for Nemotron. The documentation drift for those claims should be confirmed against the provider-swift source in the pass covering code. No concrete security regression is identified from these doc changes.
